name: PR-Cone-Casting
summary: In handheld AR, touching the screen casts a cone through the camera view, a sideways swipe widens or narrows it, and the objects inside appear as 2D clones around a ring cursor so the target can be tapped.
howItWorks: One-handed on a phone. Touching sets the cone's direction under a ring cursor and swiping left or right changes the apex angle. The candidates inside the cone are shown as flat clones arranged near the ring, and tapping a clone selects that object, so hidden objects are reachable. On an iPhone 6 with 12 participants (targets 0.2–1 cm, 20–80% occluded), error rates were 0.25% for PR-Bubble-Cursor, 1.2% for PR-Cone-Casting, 2.7% for touch Go-Go, 4.4% for 2D-Grid-Cursor, 5% for Offset-Ray-Casting and 41% for touch raycasting; times were 0.44 s for raycasting, 0.68 s PR-Cone, 1.22 s Offset, 1.29 s PR-Bubble, 2.06 s Grid and 2.75 s Go-Go. PR-Bubble-Cursor was preferred.

relationships.note: Compared with a touch version of Go-Go where a swipe sets arm length.
